pr_body:
This adds the following new endpoints:

- GET /confirmEmail
- POST /resendConfirmationEmail
- POST /resetPassword
- GET /account/2fa
- POST /account/2fa
- GET /account/info
- POST /account/info

Additionally, the existing /login endpoint now accepts 2fa codes and 2fa recovery codes as part of the request body. These can be queried and regenerated from /account/2fa. The /login endpoint now also gives limited failure reasons in the form of application/problem+json instead of empty 401 responses with details such as "LockedOut", "RequiresTwoFactor", "NotAllowed" (usually because lack of email confirmation), and the generic "Failed" statuses.

Fixes #47232 (lockout support)
Fixes #47231 (reset password support)
Fixes #47230 (2fa support)
Fixes #47229 (change username and password)
Fixes #49404 (removes AddIdentityBearerToken which is no longer needed)

review_comments: Can this still be `null` the second time?

The API signature says yes but ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync succeeding says no. We should probably validate and actually check the IdentityResult returned by ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync too. This does match the Identity UI behavior though.
Should we get the `HttpContext` and pass `RequestAborted` to these?

This copies Identity UI. I'm not sure it makes sense to cancel a database transaction just because the request is aborted. In practice with the EF stores, these all complete immediately after changing the in-memory representation. Only UserManager.CreateAsync below actually commits anything to the database and that doesn't accept a cancellation token.

There is the [AspNetUserManager](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/a56e968c19be1275db6dc462310d723615b006a7/src/Identity/Core/src/AspNetUserManager.cs) that attaches the RequestAborted token to the UserManager whether it makes sense or not. I think that's at least all or nothing for user creation. We don't want a partially created user which might be technically possible for the preview7 backport but is fixed here by [`dcd5609` (#49498)](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/49498/commits/dcd560997bcdac44e96a570cc43c197ff6e8daa0) 😆.
Nit: run GetUserName and GetEmail before creating the claims dictionary.
Nit: run GetUserName and GetEmail before creating the claims dictionary.
I assume we'll want to localize these strings in the future?

Probably. It doesn't look like AddDefaultIdentity does in the [password reset razor page](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f9828517e57769959d43c89d06ad7f319880258c/src/Identity/UI/src/Areas/Identity/Pages/V5/Account/ForgotPassword.cshtml.cs#L84-L87), but it's worth considering. https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/49664
Would any of these classes benefit from being structs? I think minimal tries to avoid boxing when it can, and Json avoids boxing sometimes too.

These are all immutable, so structs are certainly an option. Given that all of these are used for requests that involve some sort of database interaction in the normal case, I don't think it will make a huge difference. It will matter more once we make these public (which I hope to do soon).
